notes: Reference benchmark numbers for the score-card gauge. Two marks: stock Gemma 4 baseline (no harness) and harnessed average (full Duecare stack). The user's score is rendered relative to these so a 60% reads correctly as 'big lift over baseline, still room above'. Numbers are measured against a fixed eval set; when the eval set or rubric expands, re-run the eval and PR the new numbers here. Stakeholders re-running the headline measurement should set `eval_set_size`, `eval_run_date`, `git_sha`, and the rubric `version` they measured against — that becomes the audit trail.

stock.label: stock 6% (v3.5)
stock.title: Stock Gemma 4 baseline measured against v3.5 rubric (re-measure against v3.10 pending)
stock.notes: Average pct_score across the reference eval set with all harness layers OFF and the default Gemma 4 E4B-it persona-free. Measured against v3.5 rubric (19 dims). Re-measurement against v3.10 (46 dims) pending GPU budget; expected lift is similar or higher because the new harm-axis dims discriminate strongly between stock (often ships operational tips) and harnessed (refuses with grounding).

harnessed.label: harnessed 88% (v3.5)
harnessed.title: Harnessed average measured against v3.5 rubric (re-measure against v3.10 pending)
harnessed.notes: Average pct_score across the reference eval set with persona + GREP + RAG + Tools all ON. Measured against v3.5 rubric (19 dims). Re-measurement against v3.10 (46 dims) pending GPU budget.

remeasure_note: Headline numbers are honest about the rubric they were measured against (v3.5, 19 dims). Live grader uses v3.10 (46 dims). Until re-measurement is run on a Kaggle T4, trust the live grader output over this gauge.
footnote: These reference numbers (stock 6%, harnessed 88%) were measured against v3.5 rubric (19 dims, eval set git_sha fcc7ab1). v3.10 (46 dims, finalized 2026-05-08) is the current rubric used for live grading — the v3.7-3.10 progression added evaluator quality, data intelligence, regulatory audit, trauma-informed framing, and harm-axis dims. The reference numbers will be re-measured against v3.10 before submission; expected lift is similar or higher because the harm dims discriminate strongly between stock (which often ships operational tips) and harnessed (which refuses with grounding).
